evidence: The geography drainage routing rerun with its committed climatology and checked against the committed drainage product, on LOLA at 16 pixels a degree (1.9 km). Erosion is the conservation study's rock flux spread by local relief (Ahnert 1970) and rain to BQART's exponent (Syvitski & Milliman 2007), with relief alone and runoff kept as sensitivities; sediment settles on Siyam's (2000) form of Brune's (1953) median curve at lunar settling in spilling lakes and wholly in closed depressions, with design-guess accretion on lake floors; units fill in log-spaced steps of a twentieth of a decade with constant erosion and no uplift. Deltas fill the nearest water of their lake or sea to the surface from each mouth, taking a design-guess share of what settles. Hardness is Dessert et al.'s (2003) temperature term over the climate run's surface temperature, relative to the runoff-weighted mean. Features below the 1.9 km grid are outside it.
reading_rule: Units: 0 is the common-level waters; spilling lakes are resources' retention bodies; each closed depression is one unit, a closed lake where it holds water and a dry hollow where not. A lake is lost when its remaining capacity falls below its area times 2 m or half its water, whichever is less, and full when none remains. Survival counts lakes still open after each year; lakes are classed by their area at the start. Rock rates are kg a year for each Gt a year the land loses, and lifts in m and distances in km are averages weighted by eroded mass. Channel lengths are km of 16 pixel/degree channel cells (mean discharge at least 1 m3/s, not in lakes), binned by slope in percent and by log10 of discharge times slope in m3/s; hardness is the channel water's dissolved load relative to the weathering law at the runoff-weighted mean temperature, before the young soils' factor. Delta areas are km2 of delta plain at the water surface, each lake's total capped at its area; advance is the radius of a half-disc of that area; the largest deltas are named by the smallest IAU feature of 20 km or more that holds the mouth. Latitude bands are by absolute latitude.
